result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_weighted()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if the graph is weighted. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L3931-L3988){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_weighted() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns whether this graph supports edge weights. This property is set when the graph is created and cannot be changed afterward. Weighted graphs can store numeric weights on edges, which are used in algorithms like shortest path, minimum spanning tree, etc. In weighted graphs: - each edge can have an associated numeric weight - weights represent costs, distances, capacities, etc. - algorithms consider weights when computing paths and metrics In unweighted graphs: - all edges are treated equally (implicit weight of `1`) - weights are ignored or unavailable - algorithms use hop count instead of weight sum ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph supports weights, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Check if graph is weighted: ::: {#6524b2c0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec weighted_graph = ec.Graph(weighted=True) # Returns True weighted_graph.is_weighted() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: ::: {#aa697a35 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} unweighted_graph = ec.Graph() # Returns False unweighted_graph.is_weighted() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Add weighted edges only if supported: ::: {#77b49748 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(weighted=True).add_node(label="A").add_node(label="B") if graph.is_weighted(): graph.add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=2.5) else: graph.add_edge(source="A", target="B") ``` :::
